topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Motion to Infinity
target_audience: High school students or curious beginners

sections.title: The Problem of Changing Velocity
lecture_lines: Geometry struggles with constant, real-world motion.
Speed is simply distance divided by time.
A cheetah's speed changes every single millisecond.
How do we measure speed at one instant?
Calculus provides the tools to answer this.

sections.title: The Method of Exhaustion (Limits)
lecture_lines: We use limits to find instantaneous change.
Shrink the time interval toward zero.
The secant line becomes a tangent.

Show interval shrinking on a curve. (Color: #FFCC00)
Morph secant line into tangent line. (Color: #00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Differential Calculus: The Power of Slicing
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the slope of a curve.
They analyze change at a precise point.
Essential for stability in complex systems.

Add sliding tangent line at point x. (Color: #FFCC00)

sections.title: Integral Calculus: The Art of Summation
lecture_lines: Integration is the process of summation.
We sum infinite parts to find totals.
Think of filling shapes with thin strips.
animations: Draw a rectangle under a curve using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg]. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Sum slices to fill the shape area on [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/paper.svg]. (Color: #00FF00)

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.
They are connected through the fundamental theorem.
Together, they master motion and infinity.
